scripts.text:

scripts.speaker: Ira
scripts.text:

scripts.speaker: Ira
scripts.text:

scripts.text:

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh my, look at him breathing. Isn't our little pup just adorable?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Hey, buddy, it's time for you to learn a foreign language too...

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh my, look at this! Look at the way they're breathing. They're a genius at inhaling and exhaling! A true genius!

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Hello! Scania!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Maram? When did you come? You came earlier than expected?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Thanks to the adventurer's help, I came a little faster this time.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Is this the newcomer who just arrived?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Oh, that's not it. He is not from around here. He is from a completely different place. He helped with purchasing goods this time, and they've transported them all the way here.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text:
Hmm... An adventurer...? So, they're an outsider? Are we sure about your identity? What if we search through everything he have?
Or perhaps we could let slip some information over there? If not, what if they try to claim our land like those immigrants?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: No, not him! He have nothing but kind words for everyone they meet! They're not that kind of person at all. Why would you compare him to those troublemakers?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text:
Do you think someone's intentions are written on their face? Whether they're a thief or a military member, that's something we'll find out over time!
Isha brought back a wolf cub, and now, Marem, are you bringing back people?
I'm not that kind of person, though.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text:
Oh, of course, what comes out of their mouth isn't the truth. It's just talk, that's all.
By the way, a wolf cub? What wolf cub?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh! Isha brought back a Baby Grey Wolf from the forest not too long ago! She won't even listen when we tell her to take it back to the woods!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text:
Do you know what that means? It's already causing trouble for our sheep! Even now, it's behaving like that. What will happen when it gets bigger? It will definitely harm our sheep!
So, why don't you go and try saying it once! I won't listen to what you say!

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Oh? That's actually a great suggestion. It would be a very constructive conversation. But what should I do? I have to tidy up the stuff I brought.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text:
Ah, of course! Adventurer! Would you care to go? Explore this place, take in the sights, and perhaps make a lasting impression on the locals as well.
Since we'll be staying here for a while anyway, right? Everyone here is as friendly and kind-hearted as I am, so you won't encounter any hostility.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Right, Scania?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Just go and check whether what Aisha brought back is a real wolf cub or just a puppy that looks like a wolf.
What about verifying it?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Oh... well, I haven't really thought that far. But wouldn't it be troublesome if it's really a wolf cub? Even a puppy would be a hassle in that case.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Let me explain for our newly arrived adventurer. Here, the land is such that there aren't many animals suitable for raising.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Mostly, Skania takes care of the sheep and chickens. There are hardly any cattle or pigs that can adapt to such places. Therefore, livestock is really precious here.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: But what if what Aisha is carrying is indeed a wolf cub?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: The mother is coming to find her cub!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Even if the mother doesn't come looking for it?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: The cub will grow up and start harming the livestock!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Did you hear?
Where should I go?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Where did Aisha live again? Ah, right! <NAVI>[Upper Side]<INFO>wolfvill,99,178,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI>, if you go there, you'll find Aisha's house.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: But there's no point in saying it, right? If I persuade you, it might change your mind about me too.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Adventurer, then, please go and return safely! I'll take my leave for now too!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: <NAVI>[Aisha]<INFO>wolfvill,99,178,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI>, no matter how many times I say it to you, it won't make a difference, will it? If I persuade you, it might change my opinion of you too.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: <NAVI>[Aisha]<INFO>wolfvill,99,178,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> for a hundred days won't help? If you convince me, I'll change my opinion of you.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: I can't let you go alone. How can I send you to such a dangerous place alone? Of course, I know you can handle a walk by yourself, but I'm worried.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Aisha? Why are you here? Did you come to return the wolf?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: No, it's not like that. You brought the wolf... with you? In front of the sheep? Are you out of your mind?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text:
Why on earth are you trying to raise a wolf? Do you need a dog? Then get a dog.
No, I'll just become the dog. I'll mess up your house too and occasionally bite you.

scripts.text: Scania, I heard your wishes loud and clear. So, did you even send a person to me? Are you treating me like some kind of a contractor, adventurer?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Despite all your efforts, so what? This person has already sided with me! Hahaha! Come on, show me that face of despair!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: What? Adventurer? You betrayed me? How could you do that? Betrayal at first sight, isn't that too much? I should have known. Outsiders like you can't be trusted.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Scania, have you ever been to the Ice Caves? Is the blood flowing in your veins colder than the frozen water there? You cold-blooded one!

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: How can you even suggest sending this small and fragile little creature back to such a dangerous place? Its mother is dead, and it can't survive on its own.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Its mother... is gone?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I said that, didn't I? I told you a hundred times. You didn't listen again, did you? You just believe what you want to believe, right?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I don't know about you, but I can't bear to send this small and fragile young wolf back to the market.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: But if that wolf grows up, our sheep...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Don't worry about that. Adventurer?
Oh, do I need to talk about it?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: You won't listen to me anyway. You never listen to me when I talk, and you only believe what other people say.
This wolf cub will be fine if it is trained. If it grows up with other friends from a young age, it will not harm them and will instead protect the sheep.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Did you hear me? Where is your refutation? Come on, smart genius! Sit down! Hands up!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: It's true. But... but I don't know how long it will last... I don't know if it will be able to suppress its wild nature...

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: But most of all, I don't think you'll be able to train it that patiently.
I'll help you with any nervousness so you can be fully trained. I'll take him for walks so we can bond.

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: But...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: You said it was hard to keep chasing after the cub when he went for walks alone. Isn't this a good thing?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Are you sure you can take care of our wolf cub? I'm worried about him being outside with all the dangerous monsters.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: See those calluses on your hands, Adventurer? You said Maram brought him here, so he must be trustworthy. He's a veteran we trained in minutes!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh, well... I can't help coming all the way here, so can I ask you a favor? Hehe.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: You're so excited, like you've been waiting for this moment. Aren't you taking it too cold?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh no~ You're so~ desperately~ asking!! So, I can't help but...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Anyway... I need to talk to the villagers about the cub. Our little one is safe! Let's go, little cub!

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Oh... suddenly became a temporary shepherd, huh...? Thank you. I had a lot to do. What can I do to help?

scripts.speaker: Scania
scripts.text: Ah, right! Outsiders often like these sorts of things. Do you like it, adventurer? Even if you don't, you can exchange it for something you like with someone who does. Take it with you.

scripts.text:

scripts.text: Do you want to see wolf cub poop? How cute is it? Oh, but don't touch it.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Boksil~ Let's live together forever with me. If someone comes to harm you, I will personally bury them in the Oz Maze. So don't worry, Wolf Cub~ Just trust me and let's live happily.

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Woof---

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: No, Boksil. Calm down a bit. Oh dear. What will happen if you still act unfamiliar? No, I'm not saying anything to you... Let's get closer, shall we?

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Roaarrrr---

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I understand, I understand. You need some time alone. Honestly, I feel the same way. In the end, we're all alone in this world. So let's live well on our own while still living together.

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Roarrrrrr---

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Why? What did I do...... Huh? Who are you? I've never seen you before.
So this is the wolf cub?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Don't get too close to my wolf cub. Put your hands down. Turn around and disappear.
I'm not a bad guy...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I don't call anyone a bad people. Anyone who tells me to abandon my wolf cub is a villain. And I show no mercy to villains.
How long have you been here?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I can't disclose that as it's personal information. Why do you ask?
No, this wolf cub, I don't think he's trained yet.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: ... No, that's. She's about a month old now. There's no way she can train while she's still a baby.
Actually, I'm here to...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: What? I knew it! Get at least 10 paces away from my wolf cub right now. Don't come any closer.
I am not here to take her, I am here to check on here... If she separated from the pack, we have to put them back, and we have to be prepared for the mother wolf to come looking for them.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: She's not stray out of the pack, she was picked up next to next to its dying mother wolf.
Oops. It's probably nervous about being separated from his mother and living in a strange place.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Are you sure you're not here to take her away, then why are you here?
I did come to persuade after confirming whether it was indeed a wolf cub...

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I knew it! Sent by Scania, right? Why are you meddling with other people's pets? Our wolf cub isn't dangerous, so go back. There's nothing more to see.
As long as you're careful, there's nothing to worry about.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Do you really think so? Do you really think our wolf cub could be a potential threat? Look at how small and cute she is...
You might have thought so under normal circumstances, but... if she doesn't have a mother, at least there wouldn't be any reason for wolves to come here.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I understand what you're saying! But stupid Scania doesn't know that! Even a complete stranger like you understands my heart so well!
Moreover, this motherless wolf cub wouldn't be able to survive on its own.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: That's right! That cold-hearted one has turned ice-cold right down to the head.
However, for Boksil to live in the village, she needs training. She must learn how to interact with others without causing harm and how to get along.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: She is still so young...?
It should be done when she's young. If we start training it from a young age, there won't be any of the concerns the villagers have.

Hello~ I am {0}. Your name is Boksil, right? Nice to meet you. Are you feeling anxious in this unfamiliar place? I know exactly how you feel, I know everything about you.

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Roarrr---
But it's okay. Everything's fine. There's no one here who would harm our Boksil. Don't worry.

Now we're all living together. With a warm shelter and delicious food to eat.
Then we need to establish some rules. Okay?

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Woof?

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: I feel like I'm talking to a child.
Here, look. Meat. Does Boksil like meat? Grilled, raw, or boiled? You've never tried grilled? That's okay, you'll have plenty of opportunities to try it in the future.

scripts.speaker: Boksil
scripts.text: Woof!

Let's do it right.
Boksil, sit down!
Wait!
Well done. Here is your meat.
Did you see? If she follows instructions like this, please give her a lot of praise.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text:
Mom, Mom. Isn't our child a real genius?
Our Boksil did a great job!!!!
We need to keep doing this until she gets used to it. Repetitive training is important. Just keep doing it like you're doing now.

Boksil, sit.
Hand.
Wait. Now, try it yourself.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text:
Boksil, sit!
Hand!
Wow, that's really amazing.
Training these kinds of domestic animals varies. Making them feel secure in this place and building a good bond with them will help them settle in well.
And if they also interact with other friends and spend time together from a young age, they should get along well without any major issues.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Do people recognize that?

You just need to show them what you've done. It shows that Boksil is ready to live as a member of this village.
Let's go back to <NAVI>[Scania]<INFO>wolfvill,117,119,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> and show off our wonderful and majestic Boksil.

scripts.speaker: Aisha
scripts.text: Boksil is cute. But we're going to <NAVI>[Scania]<INFO>wolfvill,117,119,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> right? Don't forget.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: Why are you eavesdropping on other people's conversations?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: Uh, once again at the village meeting, all they did was talk nonsense, that old man.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text: That old man? Ah, the one whose name cannot be mentioned?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
I mean, I can't mention it.
I heard he was someone important in Rahel, said to have some influence in the Gray Wolf Forest.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
That old man, whether it's Ahap or Ahab!
He doesn't act like that when he's in Rachel~ He must have messed up~

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
If that's the case, why bother coming here instead of staying in Rachel?
I really don't understand!

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
Does she still not realize she's in Rachel?
Even sleeping in a drafty tent, hasn't she woken up from her dream yet?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
If you want to dream, do it alone.
Why bother others with your troubles?

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Who do you think you are, eavesdropping on our conversation?
Are you the Ahab old man's spy?

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
You're not even smart enough to cultivate weeds like Ahab.
So, who are you? Eavesdropping on others' gossip. Shameful.
Just a passing traveler.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
Liar. Where's a passing traveler in this Gray Wolf Forest?
They must be related to us somehow.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
If you won't speak, we'll have to use force to make you.
Are you really just going to keep lying?

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: Calm down, Redcell. Even if Zlan is not a passing traveler, there could still be someone here we don't know about but wouldn't be out of place.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: Who would that be?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
Now that Ahab is starting to listen to people... He doesn't seem like such a bad person after all.
Yeah, that's just how adults communicate.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
It's a relief that they don't end up causing too much trouble by just blocking each other's ears and shouting
Thanks to you. I appreciate it.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
You're back? What did Ahab say?
What? He said he'll start listening to others now?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: I guess he hasn't been listening until now.

scripts.speaker: Kayar
scripts.text:
Hmph... Don't tease, Zlan.
What matters now is that he's decided to do it properly.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Ya, ya.
Why did Dah... I mean, Ahab change his mind?
You must have convinced him, being a high-ranking or well-connected person.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Thanks to you, we don't have to kick people out of here anymore.
Even though he said he'd do it, it was still uncomfortable.

scripts.speaker: Kayar
scripts.text:
I may not be a representative at the village meetings... but we'll show some courtesy.
We're lucky to have someone like you.

Thanks to you. I appreciate it.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
I hope you'll leave if you don't intend to follow the rules of this forest.
You're no different. Rules are meant to be followed.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
The same goes for manners. A society without manners and rules? Barbaric.
I don't want to be in a state of wilderness!

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: Ah, it's troubling. There's a bothersome issue.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: It's a problem with relationships, so I don't want to talk to someone I don't know...

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
Would it make sense to speak if it's an important guest?
Since we can't even know about the affairs of the leaders here.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
Is that true?
...Well, if it's a secret to us, then maybe they won't tell us.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
If they're really important, then listen to us.
If not? They're probably still someone important. Listen.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
That elder... no, that's just a nickname we use among ourselves.
How can we help that Mr. Ahap?

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
He's a really bothersome old man, that guy!
He always interrupts village meetings and talks nonsense.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
He doesn't listen to others and just keeps rambling on, and it's not even useful.
He insists he's an elder, so we should listen to him, but it's so frustrating.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
I heard he used to boss around the immigrants and live off them.
Thinking he can tell the natives what to do based on his past is ridiculous.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
I just want to chase him away if I can.
Maybe if we gather our opinions and assert ourselves strongly.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Hey, even if that's true, it's not right.
This is where people with nowhere else to go gather.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text: If we drive him away, he'll have nowhere to go.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text:
But do we have to put up with that charade forever?
I have nowhere else to go either, so can I just start acting however I want?

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: If you do that, then we'll both be charades. I can't stand it...

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Hey, you there, high and mighty! You seem really interested in our affairs, still listening?
Even if you're not high and mighty, it doesn't matter. Someone with a broad reach!

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: People rarely change... was I witnessing one of those rare changes?

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text: It might still need more time, but Mr. Ahap, until now, seems like he could be a good neighbor.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
In our village, only important people don't participate in village management meetings.
Of course, the decisions themselves are made by the important people, but still...

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
So, there's no one who interferes with the meetings just because they attend.
Except for that Mr. Ahap.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
I don't like that attitude, not at all...
The longer it goes on, the worse the impact will be.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Mr. Ahab, you seem to be becoming more bearable to be around.
There's still a lot to watch out for, but compared to before, you're much better now.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Watching someone change is a sacred moment.
I should also try harder to behave like a human.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Make that old Mr. Ahab into a person.
Shouldn't a person look like a person and act like a person...?

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Is it too much criticism? ...Well, I'll admit it's a bit much.
But after working together, you'll see for yourself.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Have you heard everything up to now?
You're the only one who can help us solve this suffering.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: Since there's really no solution, if it doesn't work out, I'll suggest expulsion from the village by gathering opinions.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Geez, let's put that off for later...
But in the end, that'll probably be the last solution.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
It's not just us who are bothered, so if we propose it, it'll be accepted.
Everyone attending the village meeting is in trouble.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
But! Let's leave that for later.
Help me a bit before the end comes. Bro.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
We can't communicate with that old man.
Why don't you go and talk to him?

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Wow, that sounds great. Go and talk to him, find out why he's like that, if it's possible for him not to be like that.
It's a real lifetime request.

scripts.speaker: Zlan
scripts.text: Do it as a lifetime request. I'm saving it for when I get a lover.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Yeah, that's fine. I won't be dating anyone.
So that's my lifelong wish. Make that old grump into a person.

scripts.speaker: Karr
scripts.text:
It seems like your wish is getting bigger.
Anyway, please do it. Go and talk to Mr. Ahap.

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text: Someone who can't understand a word! Someone stupid! Someone who makes you say things again! Someone who shows emotions in their work!

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text: Someone who hides their mistakes and then can't undo them! Someone who can't take responsibility for their own actions!

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text: It's just disgusting!

scripts.speaker: Redcell
scripts.text:
Why do so many people hate you like this?
No, I hate just one person... Just one person!

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Oh, someone new. Are you a resident here?
Heh heh, it's natural for those in power to have trouble remembering everyone. You'll understand.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Who am I? Why, I'm none other than Ahab, of course.
I'm the one who goes all the way to the council that decides everything in the village, that's me.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
I, I'm also trying my best.
So please don't chase me away.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
If I get chased away from here, I have nowhere else to go.
So I've been trying to do my best in my own way. But if everyone dislikes me.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Tsk tsk, alright, let's hear about manners, Ahab.
If you keep babbling nonsense, I won't forgive you!
Do you know that people dislike you, Ahab?

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Ah... I know! So what!
Is it my fault? They mock the elders for being old!
That's not the issue.
It's your problem, Ahab.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
What do you mean I have a problem!
I don't have any problems!
You're considering sending me away from here.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
What, what did you say? That's not possible!
I have nowhere else to go but here.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
In Rachel... everything was going well...
Among the locals, it was a pride that no one was as successful as me.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
But due to a misunderstanding with the immigrant boss...
I lost all my wealth and had nowhere else to go, so I came here.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: Hey. How can I avoid being sent away from here?

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
I know it. That I have no power here.
Huh? I have no power or money now. What should I do?
You don't need power and money.
Treat people with respect.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Hmm, I'm doing my best.
I give advice to young people and attend village meetings to voice my opinions.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: Is my effort wrong?
Don't think of yourself as superior.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: But I'm an adult! Is it wrong for an adult to expect to be treated as an adult?
Then, perhaps you should leave....

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: Hmm, hmm... What should I do!
Don't shout first.
Unsolicited advice about the situation is just nagging.
Listen to what others have to say.
Try to learn about this place.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Ah... I see. Since I've listened to your advice.
I didn't even raise my voice, did I?

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
I'll try to listen to your advice.
So... please don't chase me away from here.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
I just wanted to get along well with the young people...
Was that so upsetting? It's a bit bitter....

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Anyway, thanks for coming to talk instead of immediately chasing me away.
Tell <NAVI>[Other People]<INFO>wolfvill,85,111,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> that I'll try to do better now....

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Oh, did you buy the cucumber sauce? Let me see. 
You bought the right one.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
So, where should we try to eat?
I haven't had a proper meal in that watered-down place for a while, I'm quite hungry.
But first, let's talk...

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Oh, you impudent young one!
When an elder is about to eat, one must wait politely until the end!

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: In Rachel, if there were someone like you, they would've scolded us for not learning anything!
This is about manners, Ahab.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Ahab? Ahab? No, are you boasting because you ran an errand now!
If you run an errand twice, then, oh, you'll become best buddies with them and have dinner!

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Alright, let's hear your precious words then!
......While we eat!

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Why aren't you going already? Can't you understand my words?
Sigh, the young ones here just can't learn any manners.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Hurry up and go to <NAVI>[Munomart]<INFO>rachel,135,64,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> and buy cucumber sauce!
What, do I have to give you money? Hurry up and go!

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Oh, someone new. Are you a resident here?
Heh heh, it's natural for those in power to have trouble remembering everyone. You'll understand.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Right, while you're here, could you do me a favor?
It's not difficult. It's a simple task that even a fool could do.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
It's just that someone like me has different values of time available to them.
Of course, I'm expensive. Haha!
I'll run the errand for you.
I'm not here for that kind of thing.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Oh, how noble of you.
Yes, a young person should have a bit of nobility.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
You see, there's a delicious sauce that I must have with my meals.
Without it, it feels like I haven't eaten anything at all...

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
So, go to Rachel and buy some sauce.
If you ask for cucumber sauce at Munomart, they'll understand.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
Hurry, or it'll go bad. Just get one bottle from <NAVI>[Munomart]<INFO>rachel,135,64,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI>.
Freshness is key to good taste.

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text:
At the meeting, I try to be humble.
Then the young men's eyes became softer...

scripts.speaker: Ahab
scripts.text: I think it might be a little to say that it's not a change, but an attitude, and the world is changing. There is no one who doesn't change.

scripts.text:
Welcome, this is Munomart grocery store.
What ingredients are you looking for?
Obirerger Sauce
Obiger Sauce
Oiger Sauce

scripts.speaker: Shop Owner
scripts.text:
Hmm? We don't have that sauce.
I've never even heard of a sauce with that name before.

scripts.speaker: Shop Owner
scripts.text:
Ah, Oiger Sauce! Let me see... Here it is.
This sauce contains cucumber and yogurt, so it's very refreshing. It tastes great when spread on bread.

scripts.speaker: Shop Owner
scripts.text:
How many would you like? One? Here you go.
Store it in a cool place and consume it quickly after opening the seal.

scripts.speaker: Shop Owner
scripts.text:
Welcome, this is Munomart grocery store.
It's Rachel's best grocery store, yes.

scripts.speaker: Shop Owner
scripts.text:
Most restaurants use our ingredients.
Just take them home, heat them up, cook them, and voila! You'll have a great meal in no time!

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text: I assume you must be a new villager around here. Who are you?
Scholar, what are you doing?

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Oh, oh oh.
...Do I seem like a scholar to you?
You're not a scholar?

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
No! I used to be a scholar. Long time ago.
I'm pleased that someone from outside immediately recognizes me as a Scholar.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Hmm, hmm. What are you asking about what I'm doing.
I'm organizing the collected stories.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
It's about gathering the myths and folk tales handed down to us.
It's also about preserving the precious cultural heritage of indigenous people.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text: To ensure that these stories are not lost and can be passed down to future generations, we'll publish them as books.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
It seems like you're interested.
...Are you interested in this work?
Interested.
Not interested.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
So, your interest means you're willing to help?
Extra hands are always welcome. I would be glad if you could assist.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Do you know how to write? Excellent.
Please gather stories from the villagers.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text: I've promised to listen to the stories of one child, one young person, and one grandmother from the village.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
They say it's a long story, so we may not finish in one day. We'll need your patience.
Here, I'll give you a notebook for gathering stories.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
The child's name is Dinar. The young person is a woman named Amira.
After that, you can go to Grandma Shania and write down her story.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text: We've made a promise to listen to stories from one child, one young person, and one grandmother in the village.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text: Since it's a long story and can't be heard all in one day, we'll need your patience to help us through it.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
The child's name is Dinar. The young woman is called Amira.
Next, go to Grandma Shanina's place, listen to her story, and write it down.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Dinar and Amira, did you come to tell stories to Granny Shannina?
I'm excited to hear what stories they are. Please show me the notebook.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Is this the story Amira told you?
It's really diverse and wonderful! I also remember hearing stories about these gods when I was young.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
But the names of the animal gods in this story are similar to the ones I heard when I was young, but a little different.
Hmm, I'll need to do some research.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
These are great stories that fuel my research interests!
Please continue to record Amira's stories for me in the future.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
I'd appreciate it if you could come back tomorrow and record the next part of this story.
Thank you. This is your payment for today's work.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
As much as I'd like to hear all the stories today...
Both of you, the adventurer and the people would tire out.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Take a good rest for the remaining day, and please come back after dawn.
During that time, I'll organize and analyze the stories you've gathered.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
We appreciated your last visit.
Today, we would also like to record our conversation.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Dinar and Amira, please go to Grandma Shanina and listen to her story, then write it down.
Here are some blank notebooks for you.
I'll go.
It's difficult right now.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Ah, is it difficult right now? It's okay, we can do it later.
Just remember, this work requires patience and persistence.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
We're already colleagues on the same path, aren't we?
If it's tough, you can take a break. As long as we keep moving forward steadily.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Thank you for always being willing to help.
I will repay this kindness by making a good storybook.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Oh, of course, I'll make sure you're paid for your work today too.
That's important too, isn't it? I understand.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Dinar and Amira, did you bring stories from Shannina Grandma?
I'm excited to hear what kind of stories they are. Please show me the notebook.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Amira's stories include many myths familiar to me as well.
They are stories that all indigenous people here have heard and grown up with.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
Of course, there are some differences from the myths I know...
But researching those differences and commonalities is precisely my job, isn't it?

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:
These are stories that fuel my research curiosity!
I hope you continue to transcribe Amira's stories.

scripts.speaker: Folklorist Gudra
scripts.text:

scripts.text: Dinar and Amira, please go to Grandma Shani's house and listen to her story and write it down.

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
You've come to listen to my story, right?
Oh, that's right. I promised Granny Gudra!

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
Hmm, hmm. I'll tell you once, so write it down carefully.
This is something I really experienced.
Not just a rumor?

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
What's a rumor? Anyway, please pay attention!
Long ago, when I was still young.
You're still young now...

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
Oh, you keep interrupting!
Among the gray wolves in the Gray Wolf Forest, there was one that seemed like the leader...

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
You've come to listen to my story again today!
Aunt Gudra said she'll turn it into a book later.

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
Hmm..., where did we leave off last time?
Did we stop in the middle of the scene where the dragon and the fairy have their final showdown?

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text: As the dragon summoned the giant tower of metal for the last time, the fairy confronted it by summoning the giant spirit of fire...

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
I really enjoy reading interesting stories.
Reading and imagining the next story is even better!

scripts.speaker: Dinar
scripts.text:
The characters, they come alive in my mind.
I just need to watch them like watching a play.

scripts.speaker: Amira
scripts.text:
Are you the one who came after being asked by Sister Gudra?
She made a strange request. She wants to hear an old... story that I know.

scripts.speaker: Amira
scripts.text: Anyway, I promised to tell the story I heard from our grandfather before we came to the Gray Wolf Forest.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I can't have made the wrong choice in coming here...?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: We can get most things here, but not steel. I'd like to ask for a small favor. Just 3...

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Steel!! Steel, when will it come! ... oh it's here. You're here, Adventurer. It's heavy, isn't it? Give it to me. I can't let you hold it for another second, you're a precious person. Thank you. You've done a good job.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: When the clinic is completed, we'll engrave your name on the foundation stone so that your name will live on in the lives of future newborns.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Although time passes and the building disappears, the adventurer's will will remain forever.
No, it's not necessary...

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: With this steel, I'll now build a clinic that would withstand any kind of weather, and will stand up to any elements.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Wait, what are you doing?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Are you saying you're going to build a Clinic? Now?
Calm down, old man...

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: What do you mean by Calm down? We're having an ice-cold, rational conversation. Now!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Why are you doing this? Are you being territorial about the newcomers?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Oh my, we're not those kind of people.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Then why are you so opposed to it?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: The comfortable life you want is a trap. Something foreign, something comfortable. Those things will ruin us.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Comfortable housing, thriving schools, clean clinics. Why shouldn't we have them? We've avoided discrimination, not convenience.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I live here anyway, what's the harm in having better facilities?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: No, I guess that's what the newcomers want?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text:
Accustoming your body to comfort makes an uncomfortable life unbearable. Live with satisfaction within the minimum life they provide.
They say that if you protest, they will take this away too.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: How long do you think we're going to live here, never mind take our land back!

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: What you have now is enough, what more do you need?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I'm not doing this because I'm ungrateful. They say that they are not bringing it here because this it's too foreign for them. Technology and facilities have developed over time, but you just don't understand it!

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Oh my, I think I'm dying. Help...

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Ezekiel!!! Something is wrong!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Maram? What is it? What happened?

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: If I die... put my accumulated wealth...! With me. Did you get it?! It's unfair! Maram, make sure you guard my grave well! Don't let a single penny be stolen!

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: No, you won't die. Don't be ominous.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: What's wrong with Joel?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: There's been an accident while moving the luggage. I need to get it taken care of quickly. Can you do that, Ezekiel?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Oh my, how come? I can't use one leg at all and I'm still fine.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Let me see. Hmm...

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Let's move it to my house quickly. I may not be able to use my legs, but I need to at least apply some medicine to prevent them from rotting.

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Do I have to cut my legs off like Mr. White Pine over here? I can't do that... I just bought a new pair of work boots...!

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Are your boots a problem now?

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text:
... That's right, Maram. I have a favor to ask. Can you find someone who is missing a left leg but has a healthy right leg? I guess I'll have to sell him my right boot.
Sir, please make this as smooth as possible.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I'm not going to cutting your leg off, I can heal it.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: What? With a leg that is shaped like that?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: How do you fix a leg like that...! Let's cut it off and put some medicine on it to stop it from getting infected! Don't waste time by holding it...!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I'm saying I can do it because I can do it. Everybody, get out of the way.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: You'll have to trust him. Ezekiel may not look like much in your eyes, but he's pretty good, right?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: No, the time is...!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Ahhh... If only we had the right equipment... I could have done it faster... I can't help it.

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Aaaaaah!!! I'm dying!!!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Adventurer, how's it going, can I start my construction?
About that...

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I'm trying to keep it out of the way so it doesn't affect anything else, but I guess that doesn't work either.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: But I can't give up, and I'm glad you're willing to come back and talk about it, but before then, I need to get a group of like-minded people together and get ready to convince them.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I thought about doing what they said, but I can't. I don't know what else to do, but this is something I need to do.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Speaking of which, Adventurer, I have a favor to ask.
What is it?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: You can get most things here, but not Steel. Because of how difficult it is to bring it in, not to mention you need a lot of facilities to make Steel. So, Would it be okay if you bring me 3 of them? just 3...
I'll bring it to you.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Thank you for your generosity. I'm glad you're so sympathetic to my cause and willing to help... I'll go get ready for construction.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Please convince <NAVI>[sir]<INFO>wolfvill,176,111,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI>that we need this facility.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Ezekiel, you didn't come here to live a life of riches. You came here to do a job!

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: No, but to live here as myself is to really live. I am an eternal stranger here, am I not?
That person...?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Shhh- wait a minute, listen to what he's saying, he sounds like he's saying something.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text:
No, but I'm just as much an outsider here as I am there. Isn't that the same? Shouldn't I be more comfortable?
Maybe I should just give up and go home.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: No, but that's what I initially aimed for. Finding my roots...

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Ezekiel! How have you been? Why are you muttering to yourself like that?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Maram? Maram?? That's great. You know what, listen to me. You're busy? You're busy, but listen. Who am I going to tell this to? I don't even know anybody yet. So listen to me.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I told you I was going to build a clinic here. When I came here, there was no decent clinic, so I build one.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: That's right. That's why I got a lot of things to fill it with this time.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I did that, but as soon as I started digging, the elders here stopped me. They say we should live in harmony with nature as we have done up until now, but they look at me as some sort of environmental destroyer. Am I that kind of person?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Is it really that destructive to nature and the environment to just build a more hygienic, more modern clinic, which would allow for a faster response in an emergency?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: No. You aren't that kind of person. Everyone else, but never you.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Isn't that right? And you've gotten me to the point where... I'm not doing anything right now because I'm thinking, Am I really a bad person?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: If that's the case, you should talk to Suad. That's not fair. We're all trying to live together. The clinic isn't against nature. Oh, come on.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Well... I talked to Suad... but he said there was nothing he could do and that he couldn't do what he wanted either.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I told him that we need a clinic, but we can't just push it through because the elderly people who have lived here for a long time are against it, so we have to convince them.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: From the sounds of it, so does he. We can't ignore the opinions of the elders, after all, and it's not like Suad's the kind of guy who'd bend over backwards to do so.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: So... I'm... going back to Rachel... What do you think?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: What, you came this far and you're going back?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: No, I didn't set out to go back... It's just that people are like that, they come here to have a better life, and if it's the same here or there, why wouldn't they want to stay where it's easier...

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: So what I'm saying is... I'm trying to figure it out. When did I say I would just cut it and go back? Can you please not listen to me however you want?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Hmmm... but the clinic is a necessity as far as I'm concerned, and if I can make the case...

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: That's right! I think the adventurer might be able to help us out. You know, this adventurer is really good at talking, don't you think his face makes him believable? This is just the kind of prize that grown-ups like.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: He has a big heart, and he helped us buy and transport supplies.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: He's a nice guy. He's a good man, yes, but...

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: ...Is that really the kind of person who gets the favor of the adults? They're so... so... stubborn.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: You have to make the most of it. Even if I can't persuade you, what else is there to do but listen to more nagging? Is that the adventurer going to listen to that instead?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text:
Well... Can I ask you a favor?
Adventurer, do me a favor, we really need a modern clinic here, even if it's not as big as the one from Rachel.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Where I am now, if I get hurt or sick, I have to rely on folk remedies from the past.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I have some medicines and medical supplies from Rachel, but they are scarce, and I'm not in the right place to use them.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: But there's nothing I can do to convince the naysayers, so I'm going to ask an adventurer <NAVI>[sir]<INFO>wolfvill,176,111,0,101,0</INFO></NAVI> to do it for me.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Please do, and in the meantime, I'll go meet some other people.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: How about this? Don't push yourself for a while, eat good food, think good thoughts, and rest well, and you'll be able to walk or run lightly.

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Am I alive?? Am I alive?? Is my leg okay??

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Uh, since you say it is, it must be, right?

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Thank you so much!! You saved my boots! What's your name? I'll be good to you in the future. You're my savior. I never forget his saviors. For life.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: So, how did you save the leg?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Because that's what I learned. If the clinic had been properly equipped, we could have treated him more completely and accelerated his recovery.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Hmm... Is that what everyone does these days?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Yeah, it's not going to cost you your leg, as long as you treat it right.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: You can do that faster and more appropriately if you have a clinic, right?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Yes...? Isn't that right...?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Hmm... That's the way it is these days, isn't it, Adventurer?
That's the way it is these days.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Like I said, it's not the technology of the foreigns, it's the technology and facilities of the advanced era.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Hmm, I don't think this is something you should just blindly oppose.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Right? That's my opinion too. It's about saving people. If we do it our way, we can save something from death.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Hmm... How long would it take to build that clinic?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Eh...? Well, it depends on labor and capital.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: We'll help you as much as we can. Let's build it.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Instead, it should fit in with the way of life here, it should fit in with the place.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I see... I understand it.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Wow, you guys thought of everything. This is exactly what I need, and I'm all for it.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Is there anything else we need here?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: What, you're accepting more than clinics?

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Didn't that make you think? You have to go with the flow. You can't be stubborn forever.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: I mean, we're not going to live the way we do now, even if we do reclaim our land. We already live differently than we used to.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Hey, young man, if there's anything else that's important or necessary, let me know and we'll give it some thought.

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: I will. I'll build the clinic as close to this place as possible, as you said.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Yeah. You know we're not going to live here forever, right?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Yes, that's exactly what I thought.

scripts.speaker: Old Man
scripts.text: Well, we'll take our leave. Thank you for your time today.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text:
Let's see!!!
Whoa- that's a relief, isn't it?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Yeah, it's there... right? But it's so abrupt that it's a little baffling, isn't it?

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: Now that they've seen it with their own eyes, they think differently. That's good. Now, let's finish what we started, shall we?

scripts.speaker: Ezekiel
scripts.text: Yes. But first, I think we need to change the design to match this place.

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text: The Adventurer will help you, right?
That's... right...

scripts.speaker: Maram
scripts.text:
If you need any equipment or tools, let me know in advance and I'll bring them next time.
Joel, let's go get some rest, too.

scripts.speaker: Joel
scripts.text: Goodbye, my savior. I'll be back in the near future!

scripts.text: Adventurer, thank you so much for your help. This is what I got when I got settled here, and I don't need anything... I'll give it to you, Adventurer, as a token of my appreciation.
